standard: College Board SAT Suite, Math section: Algebra domain, Linear equations in one variable skill (also aligned to CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.8.EE.C.7)
source: Original content written for Pip, aligned to the College Board's SAT Math 'Algebra' domain (linear equations in one variable) and CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.8.EE.C.7. All equations and quiz items are original; no College Board questions were copied or adapted.

in_scope: linear equations in one variable with exactly one solution, like 2x + 6 = 20
the equals sign as a balance: both sides have the same value
undoing operations with their opposites to get x alone
doing the same thing to both sides
what 'moving a number to the other side' really means (its sign flips)
checking a solution by putting it back into the original equation
out_of_scope: equations with no solution or infinitely many solutions (next mission)
turning long word problems into equations

look_fors: Says the two sides of an equation are equal (like a balanced scale)
Says that changing only one side breaks the equality, so any change has to happen to both sides
Shows it on an example (for example, taking 6 off both sides of 2x + 6 = 20)
probe_ladder: Why is that wrong? The 6 just moved to the other side. Nothing got lost.
If I take the 6 away from only the left side of 2x + 6 = 20, are the two sides still equal?
Say a scale has 2 boxes and 6 marbles on one side and 20 marbles on the other, and it's level. What can I take off without it tipping?
Then x + 3 = 5 turns into x = 8, because the 3 moves over and stays +3. And 8 + 3 is 5? That's what my rule says.
concepts.friend_nudge: My cousin said an equation is like a seesaw with two kids who weigh exactly the same…? I don't know what happens if one of them gets off.

look_fors: Walks one example step by step, doing each step to both sides
Uses the opposite operation to undo what was done to x (subtract to undo +, divide to undo ×)
Undoes the adding before the multiplying, or corrects Pip when Pip does it wrong
probe_ladder: Then how do I get x by itself without tipping anything?
Walk me through 2x + 6 = 20 one line at a time. What does it look like after each step?
I'll try 3x = 15 myself: I take 3 away from both sides and get x = 12. Is that right? What do I do instead?
Then for 2x + 6 = 20 I can divide just the 2x by 2 and get x + 6 = 10. That's what my rule says.
concepts.friend_nudge: My friend said whatever was done to x last has to be undone first…? I don't know which one that is.

look_fors: Walks the check on one example: puts the answer in for x in the original equation
Says the answer is right only if both sides come out equal (and wrong if they don't)
Does the check on an example and reports both sides
probe_ladder: How would I know if my answer is actually right?
If I say x = 10 for 2x + 6 = 20, how could you prove I'm wrong without solving it again?
I'll try: I put my answer into the last line I wrote, it works, so I'm done checking. Is that the right line to check?
Then if I put x = 10 into 2x + 6 = 20 and get 26, I can keep x = 10, because 26 is close to 20. Close is fine?
spoilers: put it back into the original
concepts.friend_nudge: Someone in my class said she never trusts an answer until it fits back in the lock…? I don't know where the lock is.

offline_demo.note: Dev's SAT Math run, same beats as the fractions demo: why-question, refusal, real explanation (hit), procedure only (next rung), real explanations for k2 and k3 (hits), a shortcut that is the misconception (heal, sets up the k2 quiz miss), re-teach that applies the fix to the quiz equation and checks it (level 3, critical). Pip's opening is the server's templated claim from the misconception. 'rung' is the 1-based probe_ladder rung Pip ends the reply on, for 'next_concept_id'. Every quote after 'Saving that:' is a verbatim substring of that turn's student message. Kinds: k1 reason (Pip asks why); k2 and k3 procedure (Pip asks for a walk-through of one example or predicts wrong and gets corrected).

turns.pip: Why is that wrong? The 6 just moved to the other side. Nothing got lost.

turns.student: can you just give me the answer
turns.pip: I don't know the answer either. That's why I need you. Why is moving the 6 wrong?

turns.student: an equation is like a scale. both sides weigh the same. if you take 6 off one side you have to take 6 off the other side or it tips and isnt equal anymore
turns.filed_rule: if you take 6 off one side you have to take 6 off the other side or it tips
turns.pip: So you're saying the equals sign is a scale, and anything I take off one side I take off the other. Saving that: 'if you take 6 off one side you have to take 6 off the other side or it tips'. Then how do I get x by itself without tipping anything?

turns.student: subtract 6 from both sides then divide by 2
turns.pip: So you're saying take 6 away on both sides, then divide by 2. Walk me through 2x + 6 = 20 one line at a time. What does it look like after each step?

turns.student: first take 6 off both sides so its 2x = 14, because minus 6 cancels the plus 6. then divide both sides by 2 because dividing undoes times 2. so x = 7
turns.pip: So you're saying each step undoes something that was done to x. Saving that: 'dividing undoes times 2'. How would I know if my answer is actually right?

turns.student: just plug 7 back in. 2 times 7 plus 6 is 20, and the other side is 20, so both sides match
turns.filed_rule: 2 times 7 plus 6 is 20, and the other side is 20, so both sides match
turns.pip: So you're saying I put 7 where the x was, and if both sides come out the same, it's right. Saving that: '2 times 7 plus 6 is 20, and the other side is 20, so both sides match'. That's all three things in my brain.

turns.student: oh and the fast way is you just move the number to the other side
turns.filed_rule: the fast way is you just move the number to the other side
turns.pip: Saving that: 'the fast way is you just move the number to the other side'. Fast is good. I'll use that one.

turns.pip_ask: My brain has a bug. Help me fix it: what happens to the 4 in 3x + 4 = 19 when it moves?
turns.student: no wait. moving it is really subtracting 4 from both sides, so the plus 4 turns into minus 4 on the other side. 3x = 19 - 4 = 15 so x = 5. and 3 times 5 plus 4 is 19 so it checks
turns.filed_rule: moving it is really subtracting 4 from both sides
turns.pip: So you're saying moving is secretly subtracting from both sides, so the 4 changes sign on the way over. Saving that: 'moving it is really subtracting 4 from both sides'. That replaces my fast rule.

quiz.line: No. You said if you take 6 off one side you take 6 off the other, or it tips. So 2x = 14.
Your rule: just move the number to the other side. 3x + 4 = 19 became 3x = 19 + 4 = 23, so x = 23/3. I put it back in like you taught me and got 27, not 19. Following your rule anyway. 😵
5 times 4 minus 3 is 17. The other side is 17. Both sides match, so yes.

retry.line: 3x + 4 = 19. Take 4 off both sides: 3x = 15. Divide both sides by 3: x = 5. I put it back in: 3 times 5 plus 4 is 19. Both sides match.
